reading.title: Are smartphones addictive?
reading.text: Few experts predicted how quickly smartphones would change daily life. Many psychologists now argue that social apps are designed to be addictive, and surveys indicate that the average teenager checks a phone more than 100 times a day. Yet other studies contradict this alarming picture, finding that most users can stop when they need to. Because technology companies operate across borders, no single government has jurisdiction over their designs, so they still dictate many of the rules themselves. The final verdict on whether phones harm young people's health has not yet been reached.
